key_insight: A Gaussian spatial weighting strategy lets PINNs automatically focus training on high-gradient shock regions, improving shock capture in low-viscosity Burgers flows without knowing the shock location in advance.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to more reliable surrogate solvers for CFD and wave problems where discontinuities move or emerge unpredictably.
method: Apply a Gaussian-based spatial weight to the PINN loss.
Increase collocation emphasis near large PDE residuals/high-gradient zones.
Let the weighting adapt during training to track stationary or moving shocks.
evidence_signal: In 1D low-viscosity Burgers tests at ν = 0.0005, the method reduced relative L2 error to about 13% and 14% for stationary and moving shocks, versus 45% and 33% for standard PINNs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how the Gaussian weighting is tuned and may be less straightforward to extend to more complex 2D/3D flows or multi-shock settings.
paper_title: G-PINNs: Gaussian-based spatially weighted formulation for PINNs: 1D low-viscous Burgers
